reference.whatHappensIntro: Snippeter is a wiki where pages can hold not only text but also live data from tables, links between notes, and a comfortable editor. Below — short, without a “developer manual”.
reference.mwsBody: The service connects to your spreadsheets via Fusion: you can pull lists, fields, rows, single values, and aggregates (sum, average, and so on). Requests go through the app backend; some responses are cached so pages open faster. You use the familiar UI in the browser — network complexity stays under the hood.
reference.wikiPagesBody: Pages are stored in a database: you can create, change title and layout, delete softly (without breaking history where that is supported). Text is edited like a collaborative document: changes are periodically saved to the server. If you rename a page, links like [[Old page title]] will follow the new name — no need to fix every link by hand.
reference.tableBlockBody: In the editor you can insert a real MWS table block: choose table, view, filter, and how many rows to show per page. There is refresh on demand and, if you want, cell editing with format checks (phone, email, link). You can also insert a single value or an aggregate in a line — like a short snippet in a paragraph.
reference.tableBlockHint: Tip: type /mws table or use ⌘/Ctrl+1 — see the table below.
reference.savingBody: After a short pause in typing, text syncs to the server — you do not need to hit Save every time. If the connection drops, a draft may stay in your browser and when you open the page it can offer to restore — so you do not lose a thought by accident.
reference.slashMenuBody: Type / on an empty line — a menu appears: MWS table, callout, external embed, AI generation, plus regular blocks — headings, lists, code, and more. It is faster than hunting for buttons on the toolbar.
reference.hotkeysIntro: A few familiar shortcuts save clicks — on Mac ⌘ is common, on Windows/Linux Ctrl.
reference.linksAndTagsBody: You can reference another page with double brackets, tag topics in text, and use normal wiki links. On save the system updates the “who links to whom” map and tag lists — so it is easier to search and build overviews (including backlinks: who links to this page).
